questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My primary wish for my exchange experience was to go somewhere in North America.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: McGill provides most information you'll need upon arrival, and their website is fairly easy to navigate. However, if I had any doubts, I reached out to former exchange students from UCPH for additional guidance. They've created 'Montredocs' with a lot of tips about McGill (best coffee places on campus etc), places to eat and drink in Montreal, housing etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive much assistance, but keep an eye at your email and sign up for events like 'International brunch', walking tours etc. The staff are really helpful if you reach out to them

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through facebook marketplace, and it was much easier than I expected.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Use fb marketplace. I lived close to the McGill Ghetto (also known as Milton Parc). Very convenient and student friendly. However, the buildings are not in the best condition

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's straightforward as long as you follow the steps and meet the deadlines, though it can be a bit time-consuming. Make sure to read everything carefully and check whether you'll need a study permit/CAQ or not

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an office for international students that you can easily contact by email if you have any questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They have a handy tool for putting your schedule together, which you can play around with before applying for courses. I got most of the courses I wanted. However, my choices weren't entirely based on interest—I also prioritized not having classes on Friday afternoons, for example.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t assume you can complete the registration in just 5 minutes. Also, don't expect much information about the courses before the registration period begins

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of the courses were easier compared to UCPH. However the workload were much higher - more assignments, tests, participation etc

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching and the amount of hours spent at school reminded me a bit of high school. Combination of lectures and class discussions

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI 342 Canadian Foreign Policy
POLI 427 Social Policy in Canada
POLI 431 Nations and Nationalism 
POLI 448 Gender and International Relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: POLI 427 with Daniel Béland was great! He was a really good professor

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Some were forced to pay the McGill insurance fee for International students due to late arrival of their RAMQ card (as a Danish citizen you don't have to pay the fee). My card arrived in time, but I heard that getting a refund for the insurance fee was a bit challenging 

Sales taxes and tips on everything

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some groceries were more expensive, others were cheaper...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost anything you could think of! The have a huge variety of sports at McGill recreation (cheap as well). Join the MOC or other clubs!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a MOC trip! An sign up with your email for notifications on other trips

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went skiing almost every weekend in jan-feb. Take the bus to NY or other places in the US. Quebec City is very nice and only a short train ride away!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - learn a few French phrases if you want to blend in when you are not on campus :) But most people will be able to speak English

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club. There are clubs for almost everything. Music, food, wine, sports etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was truly an experience to live in a bilingual city! Especially because sometimes you would just walk from one neighborhood to another and notice how the language changed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress about course registration upon arrival. Everything will fall into place in the add/drop period within the first two weeks. 

Don't hesitate to join sports and clubs! 

Find somewhere to live off campus. It's much cheaper

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to bring your warm clothes if you apply for the Winter term :) The truly embrace winter in the best way (lot of outdoor activities and festivals), but it can get really cold!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting to know a lot of other international students

Montreal is such a great city!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was not ready to go home!!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
